newsitem.title: CHINA: British protests over HK laws unacceptable - China.
newsitem.headline: British protests over HK laws unacceptable - China.

text.p: China said on Thursday that British protests against Beijing's proposed amendments to Hong Kong laws after the 1997 handover were unacceptable and unreasonable.
"We cannot accept the British protest, it is also totally unreasonable and the so-called protest is unwise," Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing.

"The British side is always forcing its will upon others and this will not work," Shen said, adding that Hong Kong was China's internal affair after the handover and no other country had the right to interfere.
Britain lodged a strong protest with China on Wednesday over Beijing's plans to dilute laws guaranteeing civil liberties in Hong Kong when it regains control of the British colony in July this year.
The Foreign Office said junior minister Jeremy Hanley expressed Britain's "serious concern" over the proposals at a meeting with Chinese ambassador Jiang Enzhu.

A spokesman said Hanley told the envoy that Hong Kong's bill of rights and related legislation, which China wants to amend, were fully consistent with the Basic Law -- the post-handover constitution for Hong Kong promulgated by Beijing in 1990.
